chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs, who said:

I heard Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying to a man: 'Do you love to remain in the world?' He said, 'Yes.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And why?' He said, 'For the recitation of Say: He is Allah, One.' So he (peace be upon him) was silent from him.

Then he said to him after a while: 'O Hafs! Whoever dies from our friends and our Shias and is not proficient in the Quran, will be taught in his grave, so that Allah may raise his status by it, for the levels of Paradise are according to the measure of the Verses of the Quran. It will be said to him: Recite and ascend. So he will recite, then he will ascend.'

Hafs said, 'So I did not see anyone more intensely fearful upon himself than Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), nor anyone more hopeful of the people than him, and his recitation was grief. So whenever he recited, it was as if he was addressing a person.'

key_terms.اقْرَأْ وَ ارْقَ: Recite and ascend (a command given in the grave/Barzakh)
key_terms.يُحْسِنِ الْقُرْآنَ: To be proficient/skilled in the Quran

ai.seo_question: How does Quranic recitation affect a believer's status in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory and elevating power of Quranic mastery, linking specific verse proficiency to spiritual rank (darajat) in Jannah. It highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt, particularly Musa ibn Ja'far (AS), whose deep emotional connection to the text reflects the tradition's emphasis on both memorization and contemplative recitation (tilawah) as acts of worship.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Suleyman Bin Dawood, from Hafs who said,

‘I heard Musaasws Bin Ja’farasws saying to a man: ‘Would you love to remain in the world?’ So he said, ‘Yes’. So heasws said: ‘And why?’ He said, ‘In order to recite [112:1] Say He Allah is One (Chapter 112)’. So heasws was silent from him,

and said to him after a while: ‘O Hafs! The one from ourasws friends and ourasws Shias who dies and is not good (at reciting) the Quran, would be taught in his grave, in order for Allahazwj to Raise his status by it, from his (current) level, for the Levels of the Paradise are upon a measurement of the Verses of the Quran. It would be said to him: ‘Recite and ascend’. So he would recite, then he would ascend’.

Hafs said, ‘So I did not see anyone more intensely fearful upon himself than Musa<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, nor anyone more hopeful of the people than him<sup>asws</sup>, and it was so that his<sup>asws</sup> recitation was (full of) grief. So whenever he<sup>asws</sup> recited, it was as if he<sup>asws</sup> was addressing the people’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs who has said the following:

“I heard Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s.) asking a man, ‘Do you like to live forever in this world’? The man said, ‘Yes, I do so.’ The Imam asked, ‘Why would you do so?’ The man said, ‘So that I can read Chapter 1 12 of the Holy Quran.’ The Imam (a.s.) remained calm for a while and after an hour said, ‘O Hafs, if any of our Shi’a (followers) do not do good in reading the Holy Quran, in his grave he will receive instruction to read so that Allah will raise him with his proper status; the positions and degrees in paradise are proportionate to the verses of the Holy Quran. One will be told to read and climb. He then reads and climbs up.’

Hafs has said, ‘I never saw anyone more afraid for himself than Musa ibn Ja’far (a.s.) or more hopeful in all people. His reading was full of sadness. When reading the Holy Quran he seemed like addressing (speaking to) a human being.’”
